title: Raw String Universally Unique Identifiers (UUIDs)
pattern: Storing universally unique identifiers (UUIDs/GUIDs) as raw `String` types across core domain models.
why_bad: A raw `String` allocates memory dynamically on the heap, permits syntactically invalid strings (e.g., `"invalid-uuid"`), slows down comparisons, and makes the Bounded Context ownership of the identifier ambiguous.
detection: Struct fields ending in `_id` or named `id` typed as `String`.
counterexample: Storing human-entered, manual identifiers (such as a username or a manual barcode) where arbitrary characters are expected and valid.
fix:
Wrap the identifier in a dedicated newtype that enforces binary format constraints and contextual semantic mapping.
```rust
struct TenantId(pub uuid::Uuid);
```
